description: Place any number of Tiles (Panels and Notes, by id) on a Workspace's grid in one call: x and w in 12 columns, y and h in rows of 8 px at the user's laptop window (1512 px wide; gaps 16 px, margins 24 px). No h means the Tile is as tall as its Panel or Note, at most about two-thirds of the user's window height (a taller Panel scrolls inside it). With h, a Panel's Tile is that tall: a taller Panel scrolls inside it, and a shorter one shows centred in it, which the Fit report mentions. With h, a Note's Tile is that tall, even taller than its text. To give a row one height, give its Tiles one h. Only the listed Tiles move. Tiles float up: y orders them, and each sits right under whatever is above it in its columns; a Tile placed on others pushes them, and those under them, down, hidden Tiles too. y is a row in the placements as the last call returned them (this one or read_workspace), so reuse those values, not ones you sent earlier: a Tile given the y of another lands on it. add_panel and add_note return only their own Tile's placement, and one placed on others pushes them down, so call read_workspace before reusing the other Tiles' y. Tiles given the same y in the same columns stack in the order you list them, the first on top. x + w over 12, or a negative or zero value, is refused with the reason, and then nothing moves; so is a Tile you can't see. A width below a Panel's minimum width is taken, and its Panel shows scaled down to as little as 85% of that minimum on the user's screen; below 85% of it, the whole Workspace shows as one column. Returns every Tile's placement. Returns the Fit report: at the user's window, which Tiles are scaled below their Panel's minimum width, scroll inside, fell back to crop, are broken or ambiguous, or leave their Tile's width unused, and any gaps between Tiles; and, not as an issue, which Panels are shorter than the h of their Tile, so show centred in it. A Tile whose page hasn't laid it out at its width yet (one not on screen, say) is settling: a later report says how it fits. While a settling Tile's minimum width isn't known, whether the Workspace shows as one column isn't either: oneColumn is left out, and the summary says so.
name: arrange
title: Arrange Tiles
